title: Stop leaking raw English InvalidInputException.reason to users; unify the diverged 6-vs-8 password-length rule
rule: EH-5 (stable codes, never pre-formatted human messages) + Evans invariant-in-one-place

evidence.quote:
if (value.length < 6) {
    return 'Password must be at least 6 characters';

why: InvalidInputException.reason is a hardcoded English string ('invalid format', 'must be at least 8 characters') and signup_screen.dart's `on InvalidInputException catch (e) { _showError(e.reason); }` (used by both _signUpCloud and _signUpLocal) renders it straight to the UI with no AppLocalizations pass — proven by this batch's own test asserting the literal English substring appears. For a bilingual EN/HE app, a Hebrew-locale user hitting this path sees untranslated English. The bug is latent today only because the sole live caller of LocalAuthService.signUp (_createOfflineAccount) always supplies a synthetic, always-valid UUID email/password — but the underlying invariant has already drifted: the form-level validator (auth_validators.validatePassword) accepts 6+ characters while LocalAuthService._minPasswordLength requires 8, so a form-valid 6-7 character password fed through any future real caller of LocalAuthService.signUp would throw this untranslated exception.
recommendation: Give InvalidInputException (and siblings) a stable code/enum instead of a free-text reason, and have signup_screen.dart resolve it via AppLocalizations the same way _mapAuthError already does for Firebase codes; extract one shared minimum-password-length constant used by both auth_validators.dart and local_auth_service.dart.
acceptance_criteria: InvalidInputException exposes a typed code instead of (or alongside) a raw English reason string
signup_screen.dart resolves the code via AppLocalizations before showing it
auth_validators.dart and local_auth_service.dart reference one shared minimum-password-length constant
regression test: a 6-7 character password does not throw InvalidInputException through any LocalAuthService.signUp caller
